explanation: Memoize the number of ordered climbs to height h. Sum the counts for h−1 through h−maximum_step, stopping at zero. Heights zero and one each have one climb when positive step sizes are allowed.
timeComplexity: O(top·min(top,maximum_step)): each height is computed once and tries the allowed final steps. The sliding window changes in O(1) per height; recursive versions explicitly sum up to maximum_step predecessor states.
spaceComplexity: O(top) memo storage and O(top) recursion. Counts are stored for heights 0 through top; recursive variants also retain at most top frames.
attribution: Unmodified EPIJudge reference source: epi_judge_java_solutions/epi/NumberOfTraversalsStaircase.java. Original contributors; repository LICENSE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
correctness: Partition climbs by their last step i. Removing it produces a unique climb to h−i, and every such smaller climb can be extended by i. Summing these disjoint possibilities yields the exact count, with the empty climb giving one at zero.
walkthrough: For top 5 and maximum step 2, the counts at stairs 0 through 5 are 1,1,2,3,5,8. Each new count adds the two previous ones, giving 8 ordered climbs. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: top is nonnegative and maximum_step is positive.
The empty climb at zero counts once.
Step order matters: 1 then 2 differs from 2 then 1.
